transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, thank you for seeing me, Doctor. I really appreciate your time. I hope I'm not taking up too much of it with all this. 

I'm here because... well, it sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud, and I don't want you to think I'm just some complaining old woman, but... for nearly two years now, I've just had this feeling. Actually, I'm quite sure of it. I believe the contractor we hired, and maybe even some of the neighbors on my block, have been sort of quietly working together to cheat us. 

It's my kitchen, you see. They're keeping it half-wrong on purpose. My husband tries to show me the receipts and tell me it's fine, and the workers always have an excuse, but I just know what's happening. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it alright. I just want to figure out why they're doing this to us.
Have you been having problems with your memory?

Oh, no, no. My memory is actually quite good, thank goodness. I... I hope I didn't say something just now to make you think I was getting confused? I promise my mind is as sharp as ever. 

I actually keep track of all the dates those workers come and go, and every little conversation we've had about the cabinets and the flooring. My husband even says I have a mind like a steel trap for those sorts of details. So, no problems there at all. 

Am I answering your questions alright? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you what you need.
Do you think it’s possible you could be mistaken about the contractor and neighbors cheating you?

Oh... well, I certainly don't want to seem stubborn, Doctor. I really do pride myself on being a reasonable person. And I promise you, I've tried so, so hard to look at it from my husband's point of view when he sits down and goes over all those receipts with me. I really have. I don't like causing a fuss. 

But... well, it's just that it's been nearly two years of this now. And no matter how many excuses the workers give me, or how many papers my husband shows me to try and prove otherwise, I just... I know they're doing it. The contractor and those neighbors, they really are quietly working together to keep the kitchen half-wrong. 

I know it must sound awful of me to accuse people like that, and I hope you don't think less of me for insisting on it, but I just know it in my heart. I hope it's alright that I'm being so firm about it? I just want to make sure I'm being completely honest with you.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. 

I... I really hope I haven't said anything to make you worry that I'm... well, hearing things or losing my grip? I promise you, it's nothing like that. It's really just the very real situation with the contractor and the kitchen that I mentioned. No voices or anything strange like that, thank heavens. 

I hope that's a relief to hear? I just want to reassure you that I'm perfectly sound in that way, and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I doing okay with all these questions?
Aside from the situation with the contractor, have you been managing your usual day-to-day life about as well as before?

Oh, yes, absolutely. I try very hard not to let that unpleasantness with the kitchen ruin everything else. I... I hope you don't think I just sit around dwelling on it all day? I promise I don't. 

Outside of dealing with the remodel, I still keep up with my church gatherings, and my book club, of course. And I still manage all my usual household routines and family plans exactly the way I always have. I make sure my husband has his meals on time, and the rest of the house is perfectly tidy. 

I really do try my best to keep everything normal and pleasant for everyone. I hope that shows that I'm still handling things well? I just want to make sure you see that I'm trying to be a good, responsible person despite... well, despite the trouble with the contractor. Is that the sort of thing you were hoping to hear?
Have the people close to you noticed a change in your personality since this began?

Oh, goodness... no, I don't think so. I really hope not. 

My husband sometimes gets a little frustrated when I bring up the receipts, but... well, he still says I'm the same woman he married. And my friends at church and the book club, they haven't said a word about me acting any differently. I always make sure to be just as cheerful and helpful as I've always been with them. I'd be just mortified if anyone thought I was becoming a bitter or unpleasant person because of all this. 

I really try to keep my chin up and be pleasant to be around. I hope you can tell that from talking with me? I just... I want to make sure I'm still coming across as myself. Do you think I seem like I'm doing alright?
Before the kitchen trouble began, did you generally tend to mistrust other people’s motives?

Oh, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. 

I... I've always tried to see the good in people, really. I think it's so important to be trusting and open, don't you? Before all this business with the contractor, I don't think I ever had a reason to doubt anyone. I've always gotten along so well with my neighbors and the ladies at church. I always assumed everyone else was just trying to do their best, too. 

I hope you don't think I'm naturally a suspicious or difficult person? I promise I'm not. It's really just this one specific situation that has me so upset. I just... I want to make sure you know that I'm usually very trusting and easy to get along with. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining myself well enough.
Have you been diagnosed with any brain or nervous system illness?

Oh, no. Goodness, no. I've never had any sort of trouble like that with my brain or my nerves. 

I've always been quite healthy, thank the Lord. Just the usual aches and pains that come with getting a little older, but nothing serious. My mind is just as sharp as it ever was, and I've never had a doctor tell me otherwise. I keep up with my crosswords every morning, just to be sure! 

I hope you don't think there's something wrong with my mind? I promise I'm completely healthy in that regard. I just... I want to make sure you know that I'm perfectly sound, physically and mentally. Is that what you needed to know? I hope I'm being helpful.
Have you started any new medications around the time this belief began?

Oh, no... no new medications. 

I just take my usual blood pressure pill that Dr. Davis prescribed years ago, and my daily vitamin. I've never liked taking too many pills, to be honest. I always try to do things the natural way when I can. So, no, nothing new at all around that time. 

I hope that's the right answer? I just want to be sure I'm giving you all the information you need. I haven't taken anything that would... well, that would make me imagine things, if that's what you're wondering. I'm very careful about what I take. Does that help?
Around the time this belief began, did you have any head injury?

Oh, goodness, no. No head injuries. 

I've always been very careful... I've never fallen or hit my head or anything like that. I always hold onto the handrail when I go down the porch steps, just to be safe. So there hasn't been any sort of accident or bump on the head at all. 

I hope you don't think I'm confused because of something like that? I know what I'm experiencing with the kitchen is real, it's not because I hit my head. I'm perfectly fine that way. I'm doing my best to answer everything correctly for you... is that what you were looking for?
Aside from the situation with the contractor and neighbors, do you have any other fixed beliefs that other people say aren’t true?

Oh, no. No, nothing else like that. 

I mean, people might disagree with me about little things—like whether it's going to rain, or if the grocer is overcharging for tomatoes—but nothing... nothing serious. Just normal disagreements. I don't go around making things up or believing strange things, I promise you. 

I know it might sound a little unusual, what I've been telling you about the kitchen and all... but it's the only thing, truly. I'm a very level-headed person otherwise. I hope you believe me? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong impression about myself. I'm trying to be as honest as I can be. Is that alright?
Have you found it harder to feel interested in things you used to enjoy?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. 

I still love my garden, and I still knit... I'm actually making a lovely little blanket for my neighbor's new grandbaby right now. I keep myself busy, I really do. I haven't lost interest in any of my little hobbies. I mean, maybe I'm a bit more distracted lately, with everything going on with the kitchen... but that's only natural, isn't it? 

I still enjoy my day-to-day life just fine. I try to stay positive and keep active. I hope that's a good sign? I really don't want you to think I'm sitting around feeling sorry for myself or anything like that. I'm doing quite well, all things considered. Does that sound like what you'd expect?
